1. Rinse tissue thoroughly with chilled HBSS.
2. Place complete full thickness tissue on staging board, mucosal side up (serosal side down), gently blot with paper towels, alternate rinsing and blotting.
3. Place the blotted tissue on clean paper towels, straighten it making sure all layers are distinguishable.
4. Dissect the specimen after the picture is taken. The steps below are an example for processing a full thickness tissue segment.
5. Using curved, round-ended scissors, press down while “lightly pinching” the lamina propria with forceps.
6. Cut strips by gently bearing down on the scissors at the deepest part of their curve.
7. Cut at least four to six strips of at least 2 cm length each.
8. Transfer strips to a 100 mm Falcon petri dish with HBSS to prevent tissue from drying.
9. Remove muscle tissue with scalpel (avoid fat).
10. Transfer lamina propria strips to a small weigh boat. Weigh the strips and record the weight.
11. Incubate strips in DTT (75 mg of DTT in 50 mL of HBSS), stirring only fast enough to keep the strips from settling, for 30 min at RT.
12. After 30 minutes, use forceps to remove strips from DTT and transfer to a 100 mm Falcon Petri dish with 10 mL of HBSS. Rinse thoroughly.
13. Using forceps, transfer tissue strips to 10 mL EM1-A tube (contains the enzyme).
14. Incubate for 30 min at 37°C bath, invert for 10 s every 5 min.
15. Filter EM1-A through 100 μm cell strainer filter.
16. Transfer the partially digested tissue from the top of the strainer to the EM1-B tube (Contains 10 mL). Incubate EM1-B tube at 37 for 30 min.
17. Spin the filtrate at 330 × g for 5 min, 4°C and resuspend pellet in 5 mL complete media.
18. Take 40 μL of EM1-A cell suspension and mix with 40 μL of Trypan Blue.
19. Count cells using a hemacytometer and record the cell number and viability.
20. Leave the rest of cell suspension of EM1-A on ice.
21. After counting, proceed to “RBC LYSIS PROTOCOL”. After red cell lysis, count cells again.
22. Transfer strips to EM1-B tube (containing the enzyme) and incubate as in step 14.
23. After 30 min, filter through 100 μm cell strainer.
24. Centrifuge the filtrate at 330 × g, 5 min, 4°C and resuspend the pellet in 5 mL of complete media.
25. Remove 40 μL of EM1-B cell suspension, mix with 40 μL of Trypan Blue and count cell number and viability.
26. After counting proceed to “RBC LYSIS PROTOCOL”.
27. After RBC lysis, re-suspend the cell pellet in 5 mL of complete media and count cell number/cell viability again.
28. Muscular layer isolation is performed in parallel with EC isolation.
29. Weigh the amount of muscle tissue in a small weigh boat and record it.
30. Transfer the muscle to a 100 mm Falcon petri dish.
31. Using #21 curved scalpel blade, mince the tissue, with a rocking motion.
32. Cut the strips into small squares or approximately 2 mm2.
33. Transfer the minced tissue from the petri dish to the 50 mL conical tube containing 10 mL of collagenase II (2 mg/mL), 2.5% PSF in RPMI (EM3).
34. Incubate at 37°C for 60 min. Invert tube continuously for 30 s every 15 min.
35. After 60 min, filter through a 100 μm pore filter.
36. Transfer the partially digested tissue to a petri dish containing 10 mL of (enzyme free) complete media.
37. Centrifuge the filtrate solution (330 × g, 5 min, and 4°C), and re-suspend the pellet in ∼5 mL of complete media.
38. After 30-min incubation, filter through 100 μm pore cell strainer.
39. Centrifuge at 330 × g, 4°C.
40. Resuspend pellet in complete media and combine with muscle filtrate fraction.
41. Count the cell number and viability of the muscle fraction (pooled).
42. Remove red blood cells using “RBC LYSIS PROTOCOL”.
43. Count cell number and viability and label MUS.
44. Bring the cell suspension from the ice bucket to the centrifuge and spin (330 × g, 5 min, 4°C).
45.

11. Fill up the column with eluent, connect the solvent reservoir, fix it in place, and fill the reservoir with eluent.
12. Start the chromatographic separation, adjusting the eluent flow to 12 ml min-1 (coarse fractionation) or 4 ml min-1 (fine fractionation), collecting fractions in appropriate volumes.

1. Euthanize mouse by an approved method (e.g., cervical dislocation).
2. Use surgical scissors and forceps to extract spleen.
3. Immediately squash the spleen and press through a 100-μm strainer into a Petri dish (ø 50 mm) containing 5 mL of fixative solution, using the plunger of a 2-mL syringe.
4. Incubate cell suspension for 15 min at room temperature in fixative solution.
5. Pipet cell suspension up and down a few times and filter through a 70 μm nitex mesh into a 15 mL conical tube on ice.
6. Add 10 mL of RPMI with 5% FBS into each tube.
7. Centrifuge tubes at 450 × g for 5 min at 8°C.
8. Discard the supernatant, resuspended cell pellet with 2 mL ddH2O and incubate for 2 min to lyse residual red blood cells.
9. Stop lysis by adding 10 mL of RPMI with 5% FBS to each tube.
10. Centrifuge tubes at 450 × g for 5 min at 8°C.
11. Discard the supernatant and resuspend cell pellet in 2 mL RPMI with 5% FBS.
12. Obtain cell count.
13. Adjust the cell concentration to 5 × 10^7 cells/mL using RPMI with 5% FBS.
14. Transfer 5 × 10^6 cells per sample and well to a 96-well u-bottom plate.
15. Centrifuge the 96-well plate at 450 × g for 3 min at 8°C. Dump supernatants and place the plate on ice.
16. Resuspend each well in 50 μL Antibody mix 1 and incubate for 20 min at 4°C protected from light.
17. Add 100 μL TBS to each well and centrifuge the 96-well plate at 450 × g for 3 min at 8°C. Dump supernatants and place the plate on ice.
18. Wash cells by resuspending each well with 150 μL TBS, centrifuging the plate at 450 × g for 3 min at 8°C and discarding the supernatants.
19. Resuspend cells in 90 μL of ice-cold methanol per well and permeabilize for 30 min on ice.
20. Centrifuge the plate at 800 × g for 3 min at 8°C. Dump supernatants.
21. Wash cells twice by resuspending each well with 150 μL TBS, centrifuging the plate at 800 × g for 3 min at 8°C and discarding the supernatants.
22. Resuspend cells in 200 μL TBS.
23. Split each sample into 2 samples by transferring 100 μL of each well to a new 96-well u-bottom plate.
24. Label one plate as “native” and the other plate as “dephosphorylated”.
25. Centrifuge plates at 800 × g for 3 min at 8°C and discard supernatants.
26. Resuspend each well of the “dephosphorylated” plate with 30 μL of the Dephosphorylation mix with λ phosphatase and each well of the “native” plate with 30 μL of the Control mix without λ phosphatase.
27. Cover plates with an adhesive plate seal. Place the plates in an incubator at 37°C for 30 min.
28. Add 150 μL staining buffer to each well. Centrifuge plates at 800 × g for 3 min at 8°C and discard supernatants.
29. Resuspend cells in 25 μL blocking buffer. Block for 10 min at 4°C protected from light.
30. Add 25 μL of Antibody mix 2 to each sample.
31. Incubate plates overnight at 4°C protected from light.
32. Add 100 μL TBS to each well, centrifuge the plate at 800 × g for 3 min at 8°C and dump the supernatants.
33. Wash cells twice by resuspending each well with 150 μL TBS, centrifuging the plate at 800 × g for 3 min at 8°C and discarding the supernatants.
34. Resuspend each well in a 100 μL staining buffer.
35. Startup flow cytometer and set PMT voltages using single color control and unstained control samples.
36. Acquire 5 × 10^5 events for each sample.

1. Use one month-old mice. To minimize diurnal variation start isolation of hepatocytes in the morning (10-11a.m.).
2. Anaesthetise mice by intraperitoneal injection of 200 μl of Cloralium Hydrate.
3. Insert the cannula in the portal vein and start perfusion with T1 solution pH 7.4. As soon as the perfusion is started, immediately cut the hepatic vein to allow perfusate to run as a waste.

Fit the flask with a water condenser in the main neck and also a rubber septum in the second neck. Place a rubber septum into the of top of the condenser. Flush the flask with argon and maintain under a positive pressure of argon by use of an argon balloon. Place the flask into an oil bath on the hotplate stirrer and fit a digital temperature probe to the hotplate stirrer.
2. Transfer 10 mL of distilled acetonitrile into the flask using a glass syringe and reusable 21 gauge needle. Turn the magnetic stirrer on.
3. Transfer 4.2 mL (30 mmol) of distilled triethylamine into the flask using a second glass syringe and reusable 21 gauge needle.
4. Weigh out 61 mg (0.5 mmol) of 4-di(methylamino)pyridine into a weighing boat and transfer to the reaction vessel by rapid removal of the rubber septum and subsequent replacement following addition.
5. Weigh out 3.1 g (14 mmol) of di- _tert_-butyl dicarbonate into a weighing boat and transfer to the reaction vessel by rapid removal of the rubber septum and subsequent replacement following addition.
6. Heat the reaction vessel to 50 °C and stir at this temperature for 48 hours.
7. Cool the reaction to room temperature by lifting the vessel out of the oil bath.
8. Transfer the reaction mixture into a 100 mL separating funnel containing water (30 mL) and diethyl ether (30 mL). Separate the layers and extract the aqueous layer with two 30 mL portions of diethyl ether. Dry the combined organic layers with sodium sulfate (approx. 1 g).
9. Filter the mixture through filter paper into a round-bottomed flask and evaporate the solvent to dryness using a rotary evaporator. PAUSE POINT: The reaction mixture can be left overnight at room temperature.
10. Purify the desired product by flash column chromatography on silica gel eluting with 1:9 acetone to petroleum spirit to yield the desired product as a pale yellow oil.

1. If using dried (lyophilized) pericarp samples, use ~0.25 to 0.5 g for each extraction, grind samples to a powder in a mortar and pestle. If using fresh frozen pericarp samples, use ~2.5 to 5 g for each extraction and chop the frozen pericarp into small pieces measuring ~4 mm2 using a manual food chopper.
2. Place samples in a 50 ml plastic tube, add ~25 ml CHCl3 and use the polytron to thoroughly homogenize the sample for ~20 to 30 sec.
3. Allow the homogenized tissue to sit in the CHCl3 for 30 min with occasional mixing by either a vortex mixer or by a bath sonicator.
4. If using frozen fresh samples, centrifuge the sample to separate the CHCl3 phase from the aqueous phase (upper layer); 1,000 x g, 5 min at 4°C. Keep the CHCl3 phase. If using dried samples, skip this step.
5. Filter the CHCl3 extract using Whatman 1 (or equivalent) filter paper and a vacuum filter.
6. Transfer filtrate to a ~40 ml glass amber vial and evaporate the solvent using a stream of N2 gas and gentle heating (50°C).
7. Resuspend the dried sample in 1.1 ml of 2-propanol. Bath sonicate to help resuspend the material.
8. Store the material at -20 or -80°C for several weeks, keeping the extracted sample out of bright light as much as possible.
9. For saponification, combine 0.5 ml of the 2-propanol extract with 0.1 ml of methanolic KOH in a 1.8 ml microfuge tube.
10. Mix well by pipetting, then incubate for 30 min at 50°C.
11. Cool the sample by immersion in an ice bath for ~2 min, then add 0.5 ml of water and 0.4 ml of CHCl3. Vortex vigorously.
12. Centrifuge for 1-2 min at top speed (10,000 to 12,000 x g) in a microcentrifuge to resolve the phases.
13. Remove (discard) the upper phase; recover the lower phase.
14. For HPLC analysis, determine the sample volume depending on the concentration of the carotenoid preparation.
15. Inject the appropriate volume of sample into the HPLC system with a photodiode array detector and conduct chromatography using a YMC carotenoid column, 250 mm x 4.6 mm, S = 5 µm, and a flow rate of 2 ml/min with a linear gradient over 30 min, starting with 100% Solvent A and ending with 33% Solvent A and 67% Solvent B. At 31 min, start washing/reconditioning the column back to 100% Solvent A by 39 min.
16. Prepare calibration curves at 450 nm with reference standards and generate stock solutions at 1 mg/ml in CHCl3.
17. Prepare samples from the standards covering a range of 10 ng to 3 µg and analyze them by HPLC. Record the retention time and the area under the curve and plot against the amount of carotenoid injected.
18. Use regression data and formulas to calculate carotenoid concentrations as ng/g tissue.
19. Perform triplicate independent extractions and analyses for each plant sample to calculate the average concentration for each carotenoid.

This situation corresponds to part (a) where the spatial wave function is symmetric. The first excited level is obtained by putting one electron in oscillator level 0 and another electron in oscillator level 1, each one with either spin up or spin down. Its energy is E₁ = 2ℏω. Now both S = 0 and S = 1 are allowed. In particular, the S = 1, S_z = 1 state with both electron spins up is symmetric in spin space and antisymmetric in space and is therefore analogous to the spatial state in part (b). 1. Inoculate *P. syringae* Lz4W strain from a single colony in 5 ml ABM liquid media. Grow it overnight at 22 Â°C shaking at 200 rpm.
2. Inoculate a fresh secondary culture using the overnight grown cultures inoculum in a new 20 ml ABM broth in 1:100 ratio dilution. Grow at 22 Â°C till exponential growth phase-OD600 0.3 to 0.4, 6-7 h growth.
3. Pellet down cells by centrifuging at 10,000 rpm for 5 min at 22 Â°C.
4. Discard the supernatant, wash the pellet with 1 ml of buffer containing 10% sucrose and 50 mM Tris.HCl (pH 7.5). Resuspend the pellet in 40 Âµl (0.002 volume) of the same buffer.
5. Add 4 Âµl of a lysozyme solution and 1 Âµl of 4 M KCl. Incubate the mixture at 0 Â°C (on ice) for 30 min.
6. Centrifuge the lysate at 14,000 rpm for 45 min at 2 Â°C.
7. Transfer the supernatant to a fresh tube and store at 0 Â°C (on ice). Quantify the total protein concentration.

8. Isolate genomic DNA from *E. coli* strain MC4100 using a genomic DNA isolation kit.
9. Shear the genomic DNA by passing it through a 22G needle 15-16 times to achieve 6-10 kb size fragments.
10. Determine the DNA concentration using NanoDrop 1000 spectrophotometer.
11. Denature the DNA by incubating for 2-3 min in a boiling water bath, then immediately place it into ice water bath.

12. Pre-incubate *Pseudomonas* cell lysate aliquots at 22 Â°C and 4 Â°C for 10 min.
13. Prepare replicas of two assay mixtures for each temperature.
14. To each assay mixture, add 1 Î¼g of denatured template DNA, the appropriate buffers and primers, dNTPs, and [alpha-32P]-dATP. Pre-incubate at 22 Â°C and 4 Â°C for 5 min.
15. Prepare control assay mixtures with all components except template DNA.
16. Label tubes for different time points and add cold *E. coli* DNA and stop buffer containing 10 mM Tris.HCl and 100 mM EDTA.
17. Add 100 Î¼g of pre-incubated cell lysates to the assay mixtures. 
18. Remove aliquots from each tube at 0, 15, 30, 60, 90, and 120 sec time intervals and stop the reaction by adding to the labeled tubes with stop buffer.
19. Incubate at 0 Â°C for 1 h to precipitate labeled DNA, then centrifuge at 14,000 rpm for 15 min at 4 Â°C.
20. Remove the supernatant and invert the tubes to drain unincorporated label.
21. Place tubes in scintillation vials and measure radioactivity using cherenkov counting.
22. Subtract CPM values of control from the experimental value to calculate radioactivity incorporation.
23. Express polymerization rate as CPM per minute per mg of protein in the cell extracts.

6. Incubate neurons at 22°C–25°C in the dark for additional 20–25 min to allow for complete dye de-esterification.
7. Place neurons in a 30°C–32°C heated adaptor, and live-cell imaging is performed by inverted confocal microscope LSM880 with a 40×/1.35NA oil-immersion objective.
8. Live-cell imaging is conducted with excitation wavelength of 485 nm and emission wavelength of 525 nm. Images are taken every second during the time of experiment.
9. Record basal activity for at least 5 min before applying stimuli.
10. Using Zen software to generate the profile of fluorescence intensity for each cell over time. 
	1. Open acquired image sequence in Zen software.
	2. Select regions of interest (ROI) by drawing the outline of cell soma.
	3. Measure fluorescence intensity values for each time point.

11. Prepare external solution on the day of experiment.

13. Prepare patch-clamp pipettes (3–5 MΩ).
14. Turn on all the equipment and set the pump to perfuse external solution through the recording chamber.
15. Transfer the coverslip with human DA neurons to the recording chamber with the cells facing up.
16. Fill a 1 mL syringe with 200 μL of intracellular solution, connect a 0.2 μm pore filter to the syringe and attach a micro-loader tip to the filter to fill the patch-clamp pipette with intracellular solution.
17. Place the pipette in the pipette holder. Put the pipette tip in the bath.
18. Once the pipette is in the bath, apply a very light positive pressure and hold the pressure in the pipette by using a three-way valve.

27. Once the recording is done, slowly and carefully detach the pipette from the neuron to let the membrane reseal.
28. Ca2+ currents are analyzed using Clampfit 10.5 software.

2. Weigh a minimum of 1 mg peptide in a plastic microtube.
3. Dissolve the peptide in a 10 μL volume of DMF and vortex for 1 min.
4. Slowly add 80 - 100 μL of 0.1 M phosphate buffer to the peptide mixture, pH 7 followed by slow addition of 0.1 M sodium carbonate buffer to attain pH 9 (typically 50 – 70 μL).
5. Separately in another plastic microtube, dissolve the calculated amount of p-SCN-Bn-NOTA in 10 μL DMF and add 40 μL 0.1 M sodium bicarbonate buffer to attain pH 9.
6. Transfer the resulting p-SCN-Bn-NOTA volume to peptide mixture and vortex for 1 min.
7. p-SCN-Bn-DOTA-GA can be dissolved in DMSO.
8. Requirement of the peptide to p-SCN-Bn-DOTA-GA molar ratio is relatively higher.
9. Requires approximately a relatively high volume of sodium bicarbonate buffer (100 -110 μL) for attaining pH 9 for the chelating agent mixture.
10. Elute 68Ga from 68Ge-68Ga generator in a sterile glass vial using 4 mL 0.04M HCl as 68GaCl3.
11. Add 820-840 μL of 0.25 M sodium acetate buffer to attain pH 4.
12. From the crude conjugation reaction mixture, pipette the volume required so as to obtain 15μg of peptide and transfer to 68GaCl3 solution.
13. Incubate the radiolabeling reaction mixture at 95ºC for 10 min.
14. Pass 5 mL of 70% ethanol through a Sep-Pak C18 Plus light cartridge followed by 10 mL HPLC water to activate the cartridge.
15. Allow trapping of radiolabeled analytes by slowly passing the radiolabeled mixture through the cartridge.
16. Slowly pass 10 mL of 15% ethanol through the cartridge in order to elute the radiolabeled unconjugated chelating agent and free Ga-68 if present.
17. Pass 2 mL of normal saline from the cartridge in order to wash the cartridge.
18. Elute the final product with 1 mL 50% ethanol in a sterile glass vial.
19. Transfer 0.5 M sodium citrate buffer in a 12 cm tall glass test tube until the 0.5 cm mark.
20. Place a 3 μL spot of the analyte at a 1 cm pencil mark of Whatman 3MM and TLC Silica gel strips.
21. Allow it to dry, then gently place the strips using a forcep in glass tubes with sodium citrate buffer and allow the solvent to run up to the mark of 9 cm.
22. Remove the strip using a forcep and cover the dried strips with plastic tape to avoid contamination on the Radio-TLC scanner plate.
23. Set the scanning time of up to 1 min to obtain the chromatogram and calculate the retention time using software.
24. Calculate retention factor for different possible radiolabeled components present in mixture using the formula: Rf = Distance traveled by solvent front / Distance traveled by the solute front.
25. Determine the retention factor values for various components: Free unconjugated chelating agents have Rf value 1.00; Free Ga-68 has an Rf value of 1.00; Ga-peptide conjugates have Rf value 0.00.
26. Cut the dried strips in two halves as the upper half of solvent front and the lower half of solute front in absence of a Radio-TLC scanner.
27. Measure counts in well counter to calculate % unconjugated chelating agent and free Ga-68.
28. Calculate % bound peptide as follows: % bound peptide = (Counts in the lower half of strip) / (Counts in both lower and upper half) × 100.

1. Sacrifice an animal with an i.p. injection of a lethal dose of ketamine.
2. Transcardially perfuse the mouse on a low speed (~3 minutes) with 15 mL of ice-cold 0.1M PBS containing 5U/mL heparin. (the right atrium is clipped with scissors shortly after perfusion to ensure effective clearing of the brain).
3. Next infuse 25 mL of ice cold 4% PFA.
4. Remove the brain and store in 4% PFA at 4 degrees C for 72 hours of post-fixation with gentle rocking in 20 mL scintillation vials.
5. Remove excess PFA by dabbing the brain on a kimwipe and then transfer to a scintillation vial containing a 30% sucrose solution at 4 degrees.
6. Once the brain has fully sunk (~2 days) the brain can be snap frozen in isopentane on dry ice or mounted immediately for freezing on chucks for slicing.
7. Mount the brain on a cryostat chuck using the cut bulb of a transfer pipette and OCT.
8. Place the empty cylinder of the transfer pipette bulb on to the chuck pre-stored in the cryostat Quick Freeze bar.
9. Place a layer of OCT on the chuck and orient the frozen or fresh brain flush with the bulb for coronal sectioning.
10. Place 40 um coronal sections in 0.1% sodium azide in PBS for storage at 4 degrees C.
11. Briefly wash slices in PBS to remove sodium azide.
12. Wash in 0.5% PBST (Triton X-100) for 15 minutes at room temperature for permeabilization.
13. Wash in two rinses of PBS for 5 minutes at room temperature.
14. Block for 2 hours at room temperature in 5% normal chicken serum.
15. Incubate in primary antibody (Biocare Medical polyclonal rabbit-anti mouse Iba1) at 1:300 in 0.5% BSA in PBS overnight at 4 degrees C.
16. Wash 3x for 5 minutes in PBS at room temperature
17. Place in secondary antibody (Alexa Fluor® 647 Chicken Anti-Rabbit IgG) diluted 1:800 in 5% normal chicken serum in PBS for 2 hours at room temperature.
18. Wash for 5 minutes in DAPI diluted 1:20,000 in PBS at room temperature.
19. Wash 2x for 5 minutes in PBS at room temperature.
20. Mount on slides using Aquamount and let dry in the dark at room temperature for at least four hours.
21. Using the 63x objective on the confocal microscope, utilize the UV wide-field laser and DAPI fluorescence to select three fields from a given slice to represent that brain region. Three fields from each slice with three slices per mouse with at least three mice per experimental condition should be used to ensure a representative sampling of microglia (n > 30 microglia).
22. Once the focus is set on the eyepieces, switch to the optimal laser for Iba1 fluorescence and range the z-stack on the microscope so that an entire microglia is located within the z-stack (~30 um per stack).
23. While imaging preferences should be determined by each user, our lab prefers to use HyD detectors in counting mode on the SP8 Leica confocal microscope. This combined with a 3-frame average provides the best resolution for obtaining clear Z-stacks.
24. Capture each Z-stack at a minimum resolution of 512x512, and enable your stack to make one slice per micron.
25. Load images on to FIJI using the drag and drop method.
26. Prepare a maximum intensity Z-stack projection
27. Make the image binary by thresholding to include microglial processes.
28. Isolate a single microglia by removing surrounding processes with the eraser tool.
29. Using the line segment tool, draw a single line from the center of the microglia soma to its longest process.
30. Using the Sholl analysis plugin, define the first shell to be 10 um outside of the cell body (to exclude the soma from Sholl analysis) and set each step to be 5 um. Select linear profile to conclude the analysis.
31. Copy the Sholl profile and enter in to Excel. Two complete microglia per field should be used for analysis. Avoid incomplete microglia or those with processes on the margin of the field.
32. Processes can then be erased and the microglia soma size recorded.
33. Once profiles are compiled for each mouse, total profiles for each experimental condition are pooled and imported in to statistical software. A two-way ANOVA should then be performed with the number of intersections from soma center and experimental variable used as the factors.

1. On day 0, collect fresh human whole blood sample from an adult healthy donor in tubes containing an anti-coagulant and keep the sample overnight (16–18 h) at room temperature on a rocker.
2. On day 1, dilute the peripheral blood sample 1:2 in PBS and invert gently.
3. Aliquot 15 mL of Ficoll-PaqueTM PLUS density gradient medium into new 50 mL Falcon tubes.
4. Slowly layer the diluted peripheral blood sample (30 mL) onto the Ficoll-PaqueTM PLUS medium by pipetting it down the side of the Falcon tube.
5. Quickly centrifuge the Falcon tubes with the diluted blood sample and the density gradient medium at 700×g for 20 min at room temperature, turning off the centrifuge brake.
6. Carefully aspirate and discard most of the top layer (about 2/3 of it).
7. Prepare two 50 mL Falcon tubes for the PBMC isolation.
8. Slowly aspirate the mononuclear layer with a Pasteur pipette and transfer it to the new 50 mL Falcon tubes.
9. Top up the 50 mL Falcon tubes containing the harvested PBMCs with PBS, invert the tubes gently, and centrifuge them at 220×g for 5 min.
10. Repeat the washing step for a total of 2 washes.
11. Discard the supernatant without disturbing the PBMC pellet and resuspend it in 10 mL of TexMACSTM medium.
12. Take an aliquot of the resuspended cells and count them using a hematology automated analyser.
13. Dilute the isolated PBMCs to 1 × 106 WBCs/mL with TexMACSTM medium.
14. Carefully resuspend CTSTM DynabeadsTM CD3/CD28 by vortexing (more than 30 s).
15. Wash CTSTM DynabeadsTM CD3/CD28 by taking an aliquot of CTSTM DynabeadsTM CD3/CD28 and mixing it to an equal volume of TexMACSTM medium in a 15 mL Falcon tube, vortex the 15 mL Falcon tube, placing the 15 mL Falcon tube on a DynaMagTM-15 Magnet for 1 min, aspirating off the supernatant, once removed the 15 mL Falcon tube from the magnet, resuspending the washed beads in 7.5 μL of TexMACSTM medium per million of lymphocytes.
16. Add the washed CTSTM DynabeadsTM CD3/CD28 to the isolated PBMCs.
17. Carefully mix the PBMCs with the DynabeadsTM and plate them into a Flask at a concentration of 1 × 106 WBCs/mL. Gently mix the Flask content for 10 min on a rocker or manually every 2 min.
18. Incubate at 37°C and 5% CO2.
19. After 17–24 h (day 2), harvest the cell:bead mixture into two pre-labeled 50 mL Falcon tubes.
20. To improve cell recovery, wash the Flask twice with CliniMACS® PBS/EDTA buffer.
21. Centrifuge the 50 mL Falcon tubes with the cell:bead mixture at 220×g for 5 min at room temperature.
22. Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cell:bead mixture in 10 mL of TexMACSTM medium.
23. Count the resuspended cells using the same instrument as day 1 for consistency.
24. Resuspend the cell:bead mixture in TexMACSTM medium at a concentration of 1 × 106 WBCs/mL.
25. Aliquot 500 μL of cell:bead mixture per well into a 24-well plate.
26. Add the lentiviral supernatant to the cells at a multiplicity of infection (MOIs) between 1–10.
27. Mix well.
28. Incubate the plate at 37°C and 5% CO2.
29. Daily check the cell culture to assess expansion, activation and transduction level.
30. Harvest the cell:bead mixture in a 50 mL Falcon tube.
31. To improve cell recovery, wash the wells with PBS.
32. Top up the 50 mL Falcon tube with PBS.
33. Centrifuge the 50 mL Falcon tube at 220×g for 5 min at room temperature.
34. Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 13 mL of TexMACSTM medium.
35. Move the cells into a 15 mL Falcon tube.
36. Remove the DynabeadsTM from the cell culture by placing the 15 mL Falcon tube on DynaMagTM-15 Magnet for 1 min, carefully aspirating the cell content without perturbing the beads and transferring it into a new 15 mL Falcon tube

## Materials and Reagents

1. Rusted iron samples
2. 1,10-phenanthroline (Sigma-Aldrich, catalog number: 131377)
3. Hydroxylamine hydrochloride (Sigma-Aldrich, catalog number: 159417)
4. Ammonium acetate (Sigma-Aldrich, catalog number: 09689)
5. Ammonium iron (II) sulfate hexahydrate (Sigma-Aldrich, catalog number: 09719)
6. Oxalic acid (Sigma-Aldrich, catalog number: 241172)
7. High pure water (Milli-Q)
8. 0.3% 1,10-phenanthroline (wt/vol) (see Recipes)
9. 1% Hydroxylamine hydrochloride (wt/vol) (see Recipes)
10. 0.1 M Ammonium acetate (see Recipes)
11. Ammonium iron (II) sulfate hexahydrate standard solution (see Recipes)
12. 10% Oxalic acid (wt/vol) (see Recipes)

### Equipment

1. MaxQTM 4000 Benchtop Orbital Shakers (Thermo Fisher Scientific, catalog number: SHKA4000 )
2. Biotek Synergy 4 microplate reader (<http://www.biotek.com/resources/articles/hybrid-plate-reader.html>)
3. (Preferred) Milli-Q (Millipore) water purification system
4. (Optional) Vertical Band Saw (for machine-generated iron samples)
verifier.reference:
1. Machine cut the rusted iron samples (~1” x 1”).
2. Clean the metal surface by washing it with acetone three times (50 ml total), rinse with excess high pure water, and air dry for 20 min.
3. Insert the cleaned samples in an appropriate container (e.g., 50 ml centrifuge tube).
4. Add the rust removal agent and then immediately submerge the sample in high pure water. The final volume should be recorded (V1).
5. Put the tubes in shakers at 100-200 rpm.
6. Collect 100 μl samples every 30 min for the desired time period (our test periods have ranged from 15 min to 2 h).
7. Remove the metal sample and rinse it with pure water several times.
8. Immerse the washed samples in a known volume (V2) of 10% (wt/vol) oxalic acid solution.
9. Shake at 100-200 rpm for 30 min.
10. Collect 100 μl of sample.
11. Add 40 μl of 1, 10-phenanthroline solution (0.3% wt/vol), 40 μl of hydroxylamine hydrochloride solution (1% wt/vol), and 40 μl of ammonium acetate (0.1 M) to each well of a 96 well plate.
12. Add the iron (II) working solution: 0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, and 90 μl to wells containing the above mixture and adjust the final volume to 250 μl with high pure water [the iron(II) concentration will be 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 9 mg/L, respectively]. Repeat twice more to produce triplicate curves.
13. Mix thoroughly via pipetting up and down 3 times. Allow the solutions to stand for 20 min to fully develop color.
14. Measure the absorbance at 510 nm.
15. Plot the calibration diagram and fit the best linear curve.
16. Dilute the collected samples to obtain iron ion in a range of 1 to 10 ppm or alternatively add serially diluted samples. Record the dilution factor (D1 for samples and D2 for total rust).
17. Add 20 μl of diluted samples to the 96 well plate mixture of 1,10-phenanthroline solution (40 μl of 0.3% wt/vol), hydroxylamine hydrochloride solution (40 μl of 1% wt/vol), and ammonium acetate (40 μl of 0.1 M). Adjust the volume to 250 μl per well with high pure water.
18. Mix thoroughly via pipetting up and down 3 times. Allow the solutions to stand for 20 min to fully develop color.
19. Measure the absorbance at 510 nm.
20. Use the calibration curve to calculate the concentration (C1 for samples and C2 for total rust). Consider the dilution of samples in the total well volume times.

18. Separate the organic phase and place it in an Erlenmeyer flask containing dry Na2SO4.

20. Fill a GC vial with the previously dried organic phase.

22. After analysis, transfer the vial content back to the Erlenmeyer flask.

2. For long-term storage, evaporate solvent in vacuum desiccator and store lipids at -80 °C.

1. Start with 2 ml of a cultured cyanobacterial cells at the exponential phase of growth.
2. Keep the cells under dim or green light to prevent degradation of photo labile tetrapyrroles, or cover the tubes with aluminum foil.
3. Centrifuge the cells at room temperature at ≥ 12,000 x g for 5 min, discard the supernatant, and resuspend the cells in 200 µl of ultrapure H2O.
4. Transfer the cell solution into a 500 µl tube, spin down again, and remove all remaining water with a pipette.
5. Resuspend the pellet in 25 µl of ultrapure water, add 75 µl of methanol, and incubate at room temperature in the dark for 15 min to extract tetrapyrroles.
6. Centrifuge the mixture for 5 min at maximum speed to pellet cell debris, then transfer the supernatant (approximately 90 µl) to a new 500 µl tube.
7. Resuspend the pellet in 20 µl of ultrapure water, add 80 µl of methanol, mix, and incubate again at room temperature in the dark for 15 min.
8. Centrifuge the mixture to pellet cell debris and combine the supernatants from both extractions in a 500 µl tube.
9. Centrifuge the pooled supernatants to remove traces of cell debris and transfer the supernatant to a 200 µl HPLC insert.
10. Perform HPLC separation on a reverse phase column using a gradient of methanol and acetonitrile in pyridine (solvent A) and methanol in acetonitrile (solvent B).
11. Use a gradient of 35% to 50% solvent B over 5 min, then 50% to 64% of solvent B over the next 30 min at a flow rate of 0.8 ml/min at 40°C.
12. Wash the column with 100% solvent B for 10 min and re-equilibrate it with 35% solvent B for another 5 min.
13. Detect the eluted pigments by their specific fluorescence emission maxima using two fluorescence detectors set to different wavelengths.

1. In the tissue culture room, trypsinize cultured cells.
2. Wash cells with sterile PBS, and then resuspend in sterile PBS to an adjusted final volume of at least 100,000 cells per 3ul injection.
3. Transport cells to the injection area on ice.
4. Assemble the stereotaxic device according to manufacturer’s instructions.
5. Lay out the drill and drill bit.
6. Turn on the heating pad and monitor its temperature with a thermometer.
7. Prepare the Hamilton syringe by rinsing in 70% Ethanol and then sterile PBS.
8. Gently resuspend trypsinized cells in PBS.
9. Draw cells to 3uL in the Hamilton syringe, carefully avoiding bubbles.
10. Position the syringe in the stereotactic device, and tighten the screw to lock the syringe in the correct position.
11. Anesthetize mouse by intraperitoneal injection of Ketamine 100 mg/kg. Confirm anesthetic effectiveness by toe pinch.
12. Wipe the mouse’s head 3 times with sterile cotton swab dipped in betadine, then swab with an alcohol wipe.
13. Protect the mouse’s eyes by coating with sterile ocular lubricant.
14. Make a 1.5 cm sagittal incision in the mouse's scalp from the front to the back.
15. Position the mouse in the stereotactic apparatus: first displace the tongue to the side with the wooden end of a sterile cotton swab, then position the front teeth in the tooth holder, next tighten the nose holder until firm, and finally place both ears in the ear holders. Once the mouse is in the correct position, tighten the ear holders until firm.
16. Wipe the skull with a sterile cotton swab to remove the shiny membranes and to aid identification of the bregma suture.
17. Drill a hole 2 mm right and 1 mm anterior to the bregma suture.
18. Lower the Hamilton syringe needle to the edge of the hole. Lower the needle 3.5 mm, into the brain. Raise the needle 1mm and wait 1 minute. Inject 1 uL of cells, raise the needle 1 more mm, and wait 1 minute. Inject 1 uL, raise 1 mm, and wait 1 minute. Then inject the final 1 uL.
19. Completely remove the needle from the mouse’s brain.
20. Remove the mouse from the stereotactic device.
21. Close the skin incision by holding the edges with forceps and applying one clip.
22. Place the mouse on the heating pad until the effects of anesthetic wear off, at which time the mouse can be returned to its cage.
23. Clean the Hamilton syringe with Hamilton cleaning solution, then 70% Ethanol, then sterile water.
24. Administer analgesic twice a day for the first 3 days after surgery.
25. Remove sutures after 10 days.
26. Monitor mice daily for signs of neurologic compromise.

1. Research representative and pathology representative are called to the operating room when resection is near complete.
2. Keep the specimen sterile for immediate tissue procurement after being handed off the operative field.
3. Under pathologist observation, remove a ∼1 cm thick wedge of tumor tissue using sterile surgical instruments.
4. Obtain 6-mm cores of tumor tissue from the wedge and place in 3 mL ice-cold Belzer UW Cold Storage Solution in sterile tubes on ice.
5. Remove tissue cores from UW solution and place in a sterile petri dish.
6. Dab excess liquid on sterile gauze.
7. Embed cores in 2% agarose for slicing, either in individual wells of a 24-well plate or multiple cores in a well of a 6-well plate with warm agarose until covered, then place on ice.
8. Once the agarose solidifies, remove the embedded tissue from the well and place on a sterile petri dish using a sterile scalpel or spatula.
9. Adhere the face of the embedded core to the specimen disc using superglue.
10. Place the buffer tray in ice holder, add ice around it, and cover.
11. Fill the buffer tray with ice-cold cutting buffer and place the specimen disc inside.
12. Secure the ice tray onto the vibratome stand.
13. Insert and secure the blade into the vibratome blade holder.
14. Rotate the blade into cutting position using an Allen wrench.
15. Raise the stage up until the blade touches the liquid in the buffer tray.
16. Set the cutting window using the control pad.
17. Step down 250 μm at a time at 1.5 mm/s until blade reaches the tallest tissue core.
18. Adjust vibratome settings as necessary for tissue consistency, typically amplitude 2-3 and speed 0.5-1.5 mm/s.
19. Scoop uniform 250 μm slices out of the bath and place in a 48-well dish containing prewarmed media.
20. Assign numerical values to each core and slice for tracking.
21. Incubate slices on a rocker for 1-4 hours at 37°C with ∼20 rocks/min.
22. Place a Millicell cell culture insert into each well of a 24-well plate.
23. Add 450 μL of growth media to each well of the plate.
24. Transfer one slice to each insert, ensuring it lies flat.
25. Rock plated slices at 37°C, 5% CO2, at 20 rocks/min.
26. Thaw MTS reagent and add it to slices for viability assessment.
27. Place 400 μL of media in a 48-well dish.
28. Transfer slices to 48-well dish, keep blanks without slices.
29. Add 80 μL of MTS reagent to each well.
30. Incubate with MTS reagent, typically for 3 hours.
31. Transfer 200 μL from each well to a 96-well assay plate.
32. Read absorbance at 490 nm and calculate viability change.
33. Perform downstream assays or fix in 10% formalin for histology.
34. Prepare slices and incubate for 12 to 18 hours before treatment.
35. Prepare fresh working solutions of drugs and treat slices.
36. Incubate slices with chemotherapy or immunotherapy for the designated period.
37. Evaluate treatment response with downstream assays.
38. Prepare GEMs or CAR-T cells for adoptive cellular therapy.
39. Incubate slices for 12-18 hours before adding cells.
40. Stain GEMs or CAR-T cells with CFSE and add to media.
41. Incubate slices with therapy, replace media and cells as needed.
42. Perform downstream assays after therapy.
43. Prepare slices for live cell imaging.
44. Incubate slices with staining antibodies and wash.
45. Image slices with a confocal microscope.
46. Process images and analyze data to quantify cell populations.

4. Prepare a 1.00 mM MDA working solution with 100 mM 1,1,3,3-tetraethoxypropane stock solution diluted to 100 ml with ultrapure water; mix well.
5. Prepare an MDA calibration curve by serial dilution of the freshly prepared working solution.
6. Store standards on ice until use.
7. Thaw plasma samples on ice and spin at 3,000 x g and 4°C for 1 min to collect plasma.
8. Label standard 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tubes for samples and standards.
9. Transfer 20 µl of each standard or plasma sample to labeled tubes.
10. Add 2 µl BHT solution and 5 µl of 2 N NaOH solution to each tube.
11. Vortex briefly, then incubate at 60°C for 30 min with 400 rpm agitation in a shaking dry block incubator.
12. Transfer tubes to ice, add 100 µl of 15% trichloroacetic acid to precipitate proteins, briefly vortex and incubate for 5 min on ice.
13. Centrifuge tubes at 14,000 x g and 4°C for 10 min to pellet the protein.
14. Transfer 100 µl of supernatant to a fresh 500 µl screw cap microcentrifuge tube without disturbing the pellet.
15. Add 50 µl of 2-thiobarbituric acid derivatizing solution, seal the caps, and incubate at 100°C for 60 min in a dry block incubator.
16. Cool the tubes in an ice bath, then centrifuge at 14,000 x g and 4°C for 5 min.
17. Transfer 60 µl of the derivatized solution to a microinsert HPLC vial.
18. Subject the vials to HPLC analysis within 12 h.
19. Prepare iron sulfate working solution by diluting 1 ml of 300 mM stock with 9 ml of distilled water.
20. Plan the layout of samples and calibration curve on a standard flat-bottomed 96-well plate.

22. Incubate for 5 min at room temperature at 100 rpm on an orbital shaker.

1. Wash crystal quartzes three times with ethanol.
2. Dry them with Argon.
3. Incubate them overnight at 4°C with 2 mM cysteamine.
4. Wash quartzes again three times with ethanol to remove any unbound cysteamine.
5. Dry quartzes with Argon.
6. Transform plasmids DNA coding for GST tagged proteins into Escherichia coli.
7. Purify DNA using the NucleoPrepII anion exchange resin (Macherey Nagel).
8. Prepare NAPPA printing mix with 1.4 μg/ul DNA, 3.75 μg/ul BSA (Sigma-Aldrich), 5 mM BS3 (Pierce, Rockford, IL, USA) and 66.5 μg polyclonal capture GST antibody (GE Healthcares).
9. Prepare negative controls, named master mix (MM), replacing DNA for water in the printing mix.
10. Incubate samples at room temperature for 1 hour with agitation.
11. Print them on the cysteamine-coated gold quartz using the Qarray II from Genetix.
12. Perform in vitro transcription and translation (IVTT) using HeLa lysate mix (1-Step Human Coupled IVTT Kit, Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc.), according to the manufacturers’ instructions.
13. Incubate the quartz, connected to the nanogravimeter inside the incubator, for 10 min at 30°C with 40 μl of HeLa lysate mix for proteins synthesis.
14. Acquire the conductance curve (“IVTT addition curve”, prior protein expression).
15. Decrease the temperature to 15°C for a period of 5-10 min to facilitate the proteins binding on the capture antibody (anti-GST).
16. Acquire the conductance curve (“IVTT addition at 10 min”, after protein expression).
17. After the protein expression and capture, remove the quartzes from the instrument and wash at room temperature, in 500 mM NaCl PBS for 3 times.
18. After protein expression, capture, wash the quartzes in PBS at increasing concentrations at 22°C.
19. Acquire the conductance curve (“Post-wash curve”, after the final washing process with PBS).

Consider two nonrelativistic, noninteracting spin-1/2 fermions each of mass m in an infinite square well potential of length L between x = −L/2 and x = L/2. verifier.reference: Since there is no interaction and no spin-dependence in the Hamiltonian, the energy eigenvalues are determined solely by the spatial degree of freedom x, and the many-body states will be appropriately antisymmetrized combinations of the single-particle states. The boundary conditions for the single-particle wave function ψ(x) in an infinite square well between x = −L/2 and x = L/2 are ψ(−L/2) = ψ(L/2) = 0. The normalized single-particle eigenstates are given by ψn(x) = √(2/L) { cos(πnx/L) for n odd, sin(πnx/L) for n even }. The corresponding eigenvalues are ϵn = ℏ²π²n²/2mL². We label these single-particle eigenstates as |n⟩i, where i = 1, 2 labels the particle. The two-particle wave function can be expressed as a product of a spatial wave function and a spin wave function. The total wave function must be antisymmetric under the exchange of the two particles. Thus, when the spatial wave function is symmetric, the spin wave function must be antisymmetric and vice versa. The lowest two-particle eigenstate corresponds to both particles in the lowest spatial single-particle state n = 1 and its energy is E = 2ϵ1 = ℏ²π²/mL². The corresponding spatial wave function |1⟩1|1⟩2 is symmetric, hence the spin wave function must be antisymmetric (i.e., a singlet). The complete normalized ground-state wave function is (|1⟩1|1⟩2) 1/√2 (| ↑⟩1| ↓⟩2 −| ↓⟩1| ↑⟩2). The next lowest two-particle states will involve particles in the spatial single-particle states n = 1 and n = 2 with total energy of E = ϵ1 + ϵ2 = 5ℏ²π²/2mL². These could be combined into a symmetric spatial wave function, which would require an antisymmetric (i.e., singlet) spin wave function 1/√2 (|1⟩1|2⟩2 + |2⟩1|1⟩2) 1/√2 (| ↑⟩1| ↓⟩2 −| ↓⟩1| ↑⟩2), or they could be combined into an antisymmetric spatial wave function, which would require a symmetric (i.e., triplet) spin wave function. Note that there are three symmetric spin wave functions giving three two-particle eigensates 1/√2 (|1⟩1|2⟩2 −|2⟩1|1⟩2) (| ↑⟩1| ↑⟩2), 1/√2 (|1⟩1|2⟩2 −|2⟩1|1⟩2) 1/√2 (| ↑⟩1| ↓⟩2 + | ↓⟩1| ↑⟩2), 1/√2 (|1⟩1|2⟩2 −|2⟩1|1⟩2) (| ↓⟩1| ↓⟩2). These last four states all have the same energy E = ϵ1 + ϵ2. The next lowest energy state will have both particles in n = 2 giving an energy of 2ϵ2 > ϵ1 + ϵ2. Thus the five states listed above are the five lowest energy eigenstates.

verifier.reference: The quadrupole moment for this configuration vanishes by symmetry. To see this, we note that in the definition of Q_{ij}, the δ_{ij} term vanishes since the sum of the charges is zero, and they are all equidistant from the origin. The r'_i r'_j term vanishes since for every charge, there is an opposite charge in the mirrored position r_i → -r_i, r_j → -r_j. The mirroring does not change the sign of the bilinear r_i r_j, so the mirrored charges all cancel in the sum defining the quadrupole moment. However, this configuration has a non-trivial octupole moment. We therefore expect that the potential will fall off as 1/r⁴.

2. Grind kernels into powder using a mortar and pestle within liquid nitrogen.
3. Transfer the powder into a 2 ml eppendorf tube. Dry it in Concentrator plus for 1 h till achieve constant weight.
4. Add 1 ml petroleum ether. Vortex and place in the shaker at 250 rpm for 1 h.
5. Centrifuge for 15 min at 12,000 rpm at room temperature (RT), and discard the supernatant.
6. Dry it in Concentrator Plus for 1.5 h until no smell of organic liquid is detectable.
7. Fill a new 2 ml Eppendorf tube with 50 mg dried powder from the step 6.

9. Centrifuge for 15 min at 12,000 rpm at RT.
10. Transfer 300 Î¼l supernatant into a new 2 ml eppendorf tube as total protein extraction (Fraction A).
11. Transfer another 300 Î¼l supernatant from the step 9 into a new 2 ml Eppendorf tube, and add 700 Î¼l ethanol as well as 1% PMSF. Mix with shaking at 250 rpm for 2 h at RT.
12. Centrifuge product from step 11 for 15 min at 12,000 rpm at RT.
13. Transfer 400-500 Î¼l supernatant into a new 2 ml Eppendorf tube and dry it in Concentrator plus for 2-3 h. Resuspend it in 200 Î¼l IPG as zein proteins extraction (Fraction B).
14. Wash the precipitate in step 12 with 70% ethanol twice.
15. Centrifuge for 15 min at 12,000 rpm at RT.
16. Discard the supernatant and air-dry the precipitate until the edges become transparent. Resuspend it in 200 Î¼l IPG as non-zein proteins extraction (Fraction C).
17. Add 10 Î¼l protein extraction from fraction A, or B, or C, 1.5 Î¼l DTT and 3 Î¼l 5x Protein loading buffer in a new 0.2 ml eppendorf tube. Heat 10 min at 99 Â°C for denaturation.
18. Load 2-5 Î¼l denatured protein sample and perform the SDS-PAGE on a 15% separation gel.
19. The gel is stained with Coomassie brilliant blue R250.
20. Soak 3-5 mature corn kernels in ddH2O for 10 min, then remove the pericarp and embryo and dry the kernels for 10 min at 37 Â°C.
21. Grind kernels into powder using a mortar and pestle within liquid nitrogen.
22. Transfer the powder into a 2 ml eppendorf tube. Dry it in Concentrator plus for 1 h till achieve constant weight.
23. Fill a new 2 ml eppendorf tube with 50 mg dry powder from step 22.
24. Add 400 Î¼l 70% ethanol and 8 Î¼l Î²-mercaptoethanol as well as 1% PMSF.
25. Mix and incubate for at least 2 h at RT. Invert the cube 2-3 times during incubation.
26. Centrifuge for 10 min at 1,300 rpm at RT.
27. Transfer 100 Î¼l supernatant into a new 2 ml eppendorf tube.
28. Add 10 Î¼l 10% SDS, and mix by pipetting.
29. Dry it in Concentrator plus for 1 h.
30. Add 200 Î¼l ddH2O for elution.

1. Design and order sgRNA oligos as follows: Forward: 5’ CACC+”20 bp sgRNA sequence” 3’, Reverse: 5’ AAAC+”reverse complement of the 20 bp sgRNA sequence” 3’.

3. Prepare the oligo annealing reaction in a PCR tube, heat in thermocycler for 5 min at 95°C and gradually ramp down to 20°C at 5°C/min. Dilute annealed oligos 1:20 in ddH2O before ligation reaction.
4. Prepare the ligation reaction in a 0.2 mL PCR tube. Perform ligation at 20°C–25°C for 1 h using the Quick Ligation kit.
5. Transform 3 μL of the ligation reaction into a competent E. coli strain and plate the reaction on agar plates containing ampicillin for antibiotic selection.
6. Inoculate 1.5 mL of TB medium containing 100 μg/mL ampicillin with a single colony picked with a sterile pipette tip. Incubate and shake cultures at 37°C for 16–18 h.
7. Perform plasmid isolation using a QIAprep spin miniprep kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
8. Verify the correctly cloned sgRNA sequence by Sanger sequencing with eSpCas9-forward primer.
9. Design donor plasmid following guidelines for structure and include homology arms, selection markers, and the dTAG degron tag, ensuring all fragments require a sequence homology of 15 bp for sequential In-Fusion assembly.
10. Amplify the selection cassette by PCR and isolate DNA with a gel extraction kit after running the reaction on a 0.8% agarose gel.
11. Linearize donor plasmid backbone with Eco53kI and isolate backbone DNA from the gel using the QIAquick PCR and gel cleanup kit.
12. Prepare the In-Fusion HD cloning reaction for targeting vector assembly and perform diagnostic colony PCR if necessary.
13. Inoculate at least 2 PCR-positive colonies into 1.5 mL LB or TB medium containing 100 μg/mL ampicillin. Incubate culture while shaking at 37°C for 16–18 h.
14. Isolate plasmid DNA using a QIAprep spin miniprep kit.
15. Perform validation of donor plasmids by Sanger sequencing.
16. For plasmid-based delivery into mouse ES cells, plate cells and prepare for lipofection or for difficult to transfect cell lines, proceed with nucleofection of preassembled Cas9/gRNA ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complex.

1. The precursors used to prepare Ag nanoparticles are GG and silver nitrate.
2. 2.5 %w/v of GG was dissolved in 10 ml distilled water with the help of magnetic stirrer.
3. After complete dissolution, the temperature of the reaction medium is raised to 70 oC.
4. 10 ml of 15 mM silver nitrate solution was then added drop wise to the solution.
5. The reaction mixture was kept under continuous stirring for 90 min.
6. The synthesis takes place at pH 6.
7. Short time after addition of silver nitrate solution, the reaction medium acquires a clear yellow color indicating the formation of Ag nanoparticles.
8. In order to make the double loading, 30 mM silver nitrate were used at the identical condition.
9. The GG/Ag nanocomposite was characterized by XRD operating in the reflection mode with CuKα radiation.
10. The morphology of the films was investigated by SEM.
11. The size and shape of the nanoparticles were obtained using TEM.
12. For TEM studies, the samples were prepared by drop-casting dispersed colloidal solution on a carbon-coated copper grid.
13. FTIR spectra were recorded to confirm the presence of the required functional groups in the GG and GG/Ag nanocomposite.
14. Normal (film I) and double loaded films (film II) were prepared by drop-casting 15 mM and 30 mM GG/Ag nanocomposite solution on flexible transparency slide (1cm x 1cm) followed by dried in air.
15. For electrical characterization, film I & II were electrically connected to a copper wire as electrodes with the help of silver paste.
16. Electrical measurements were taken with an Agilent SMU as voltage-source and current-meter.
17. Electrical conductivity of GG film, film I & II were carried out.
18. XPS and field-effect transistor (FET) analysis has been carried out in order to confirm the sensing mechanism.
19. Upon exposure to aqueous ammonia of different concentrations, the conductivity of GG/Ag nanocomposite film is found to increase.
20. Aqueous ammonia sensing experiments were carried out in a simple home-made testing chamber.
21. The ammonia vapors of different concentrations were introduced into the testing chamber manually at the humidity of ~48% and temperature of 20-25 0C.
22. In order to understand the sensing mechanism, sensing experiments under different environmental conditions (ambient, oxygen and nitrogen) and studied the FET characteristics of the sensing film on a Si/SiO2 substrate were conducted.
23. The kinetics of a chemical reaction such as generation of ammonia from hexamethylenetetramine (HMT) in water at different temperatures is studied by the sensing film.

7. Add 400 Âµl of extraction buffer.
8. Add 20 Âµl of internal standard.
9. Vigorously shake for 15 min on a vortexer at room temperature.

13. Add 200 Âµl of 1 M sodium hydroxide.
14. Add 167 Âµl of methanol and 34 Âµl of pyridine.
15. Vortex vigorously and break up any pellets with a Pasteur pipette.

17. Add another 20 Âµl of propyl chloroformate and vigorously vortex for 30 s.
18. Add 400 Âµl of chloroform and vortex vigorously for 10 s.
19. Add 400 Âµl of sodium bicarbonate (50 mM) and vortex vigorously for 10 s.

21. The lower layer is transferred to a new 13 x 100 mm glass test tube with a Pasteur pipet.
22. Dry the chloroform extract by adding approximately 40 Âµl of anhydrous sodium sulfate and vortex until clear.
23. Centrifuge for 1 min with a table-top swing-arm centrifuge at about 80% speed (approximately 1,250 *x g*).
24. Transfer chloroform extract to a GC vial with a Pasteur pipet.

1. Grow two strains of cells, one of which expresses a fluorescent nucleolar protein. One is MAT a and the other is MAT α.
2. Combine aliquots of both parental cells (e.g., 100 μL of each). Vortex.
3. Sediment the cell mixtures and resuspend in synthetic medium with 2% glucose at OD600 ≈ 1.
4. Apply 25 μL samples of these mating mixtures to the surface of Petri dishes containing solid 2% agar in synthetic medium.
5. Leave open in a laminar-flow hood. Liquid should be absorbed in < 15 min. The dishes are then covered. The overall timing of the cross is measured from the moment when the mating mixture is applied to the surface of the Petri dish.
6. After 2 h at room temperature, recover the cell mixture by washing with synthetic medium and gentle pipetting up and down 4–5×.
7. Sediment the cells. Without removing the supernatant, recover 0.5–1.0 μL samples of the cell pellet and apply this volume to the surface of freshly-opened Agarose pads, cover with a coverslip, and observe.
8. To restrict attention to relatively early events, examine zygotes that show no sign of bud emergence that coincides with onset of DNA synthesis and focus on early zygotes that show evidence of nuclear fusion.
9. Pregrow one or both parental cells that express a tagged protein of interest from a repressible promoter, using a medium that allows expression (e.g., with galactose or lacking methionine).
10. When the mating mixture is prepared, adjust the composition of the plate used for the cross to repress transcription, e.g., by addition of glucose or methionine.
11. Pipette the mating mixture off the plate with complete medium.
12. Add 1/10 volume of formaldehyde from a 37% stock in water, shaking for 5 min at room temperature.
13. Wash once with growth medium to quench free aldehydes.
14. Include a marker of the lumen of the nuclear envelope and ER (either mRFP-HDEL or GFP-HDEL) in crossings.
15. Judge the possible contribution of nucleocytoplasmic shuttling and new synthesis by following GFP-tagged AFs in crosses with a *kar1Δ15* mutant.
16. Collect images of 3−10 fields and examine at least 25 zygotes per cross using a Deltavision RT epifluorescence microscope.
17. Use an oil immersion objective (Olympus UPlanApo 100×/1.40; ∞/0.17/FN26.5).
18. Capture z-stacks at 0.5–1.0 μm intervals using a CCD digital camera.
19. Examine through-focal series spanning a total of 6 μ in all cases.
20. Remove out-of-focus light using the Softworks deconvolution program.
21. Repeat experiments 2–4 ×.

1. Incubate 3ul PCR reaction to be sequenced with 1ul ExoSAP for 15’ at 37ºC in duplicate for one forward and one reverse reaction.
2. Inactivate the enzyme 15’ at 80ºC.
3. Add 2 ul of 1-2 uM primer, 2 uL of 5x Applied Biosystems BigDye buffer, 1 ul of ABI-supplied BigDye mix to each tube, and bring the final volume to 10 ul with ddH2O.
4. Centrifuge briefly and cycle using the terminator program.
5. Proceed with the spin column purification using G-50 microtiter plate procedures.
   a. Add dry Sephadex G-50 to the Millipore 45 ul Column Loader.
   b. Remove the excess of resin from the top of the Column Loader with the scraper.
   c. Place MultiScreen HV Plate upside-down on top of the Column Loader.
   d. Invert both MultiScreen HV Plate and Column Loader and tap to release the resin.
   e. Using a multi-channel pipettor, add 300 ul of ddH2O to each well to swell the resin and let stand at room temperature for 1-3 hours.
   f. Seal swollen minicolumns with saran wrap and store at 4 deg C if necessary.
6. Spin through excess liquid over a reserved collection plate by centrifuging for 5’ at 2000 rpm.
7. Add 20 ul ddH20 to each reaction before applying to columns. Align over clean collection tubes, spin 5’ at 2500 rpm, and recover approx. 20 ul. Freeze if not sequencing that day.
8. Run sequences on the automated sequencer.

12. Fix the PFFs sample on the grid using 2% PFA for 10 min at room temperature.
13. Remove PFA drop using filter paper.
14. Add one drop of ddH2O onto the grid for 1 min at room temperature, then remove with filter paper and repeat once more.
15. Stain the grid with Uranyless, centrifuged at 14,000 x g, and add one drop of the supernatant to the grid for 5 min at room temperature.
16. Wash the grid with ddH2O and remove the drop using Whatman filter paper.
17. Let the grid sit overnight on parafilm at room temperature, placed in a box/chamber to avoid contaminants.
18. Wash wells of 8-well Permanox plates with 100% ethanol three times, then with ddH2O three times.
19. Add 200 μL of 0.01% poly-L-lysine to each well and incubate for 1 h at 37°C.
20. Wash wells three times with ddH2O.
21. Trypsinize U2OS cells, pellet, remove supernatant, resuspend in growth media and plate approximately 50,000 cells per well with 150-200 μL of media.
22. Incubate cells for 48-72 h.
23. Add 5 μL of conjugated PFFs to each well and incubate for 30 min at 37°C.
24. Remove cell media.
25. Optionally administer 200 μL of ice-cold trypsin to each well, incubate for 60-90 s on ice, remove trypsin, and wash cells with 200 μL of ice-cold PBS.
26. Fix cells with 2.5% glutaraldehyde supplemented with 2 mM CaCl2 at 4°C overnight.
27. Wash cells with 0.1 mM sodium cacodylate buffer by aspirating the buffer, adding 200 μL to each well, aspirating again, and replacing with fresh buffer.

36. Trim and section prepared blocks, then place one section onto a grid using the Perfect Loop tool and let it dry.
37. Stain sections with uranyl acetate and lead citrate.
38. Image grids using a transmission electron microscope at magnifications between ×9300 and ×18500.

1. Warm enzyme solutions (50 µl) to RT and dilute to 500 µl with storage buffer. 
2. Store aliquots (5 µl) at -80 °C until needed.
3. Dissolve Heparin or HS (1 mg) in a microcentrifuge tube (1.5 ml) with digestion media (470 µl).
4. Add HL I (5 µl) to the solution and incubate (37 °C, 2 h, inversion at 9 rpm).
5. Add HL III (5 µl) to the solution and continue incubation (1 h).
6. Add HL II (5 µl) to the solution and incubate (18 h).
7. Add all three enzymes (5 µl each) and incubate with gentle inversion (9 rpm) for 24 h.
8. Terminate digests by heating (100 °C, 5 min).
9. Centrifuge samples (14,000 x g, 10 min) and recover the supernatant.
10. Dilute the supernatants to 100 µg/ml with water, by taking 50 µl supernatant and adding 950 µl water.
11. Filter the solutions (0.22 µm) before analysis.
12. Condition the HPLC column by flushing with water, then with 100% B for 10 min and equilibrate with 0% B for 2 min.
13. Inject the digests and standard solutions (50 µl injection volume) into the HPLC.
14. Apply a gradient system to separate disaccharides with the binary solvent system at 1 ml/min and 40 °C.
15. Detect disaccharides by absorbance at 232 nm.
16. Prepare standard curves by first dissolving heparin-derived disaccharide standards to 1 mg/ml, then dilute to prepare various standard concentrations.
17. Analyze standard solutions and compare sample digests to generate calibration curves and quantify the disaccharides present.

1. Collect macrophages from petri dishes:
   1.1. Aspirate supernatant.
   1.2. Wash adherent macrophages with PBS, using a gentle rinse once for mouse macrophages, or a more forceful rinse three times for human macrophages. 
   1.3. Add 5 mL of trypsin per plate and incubate at 37°C for up to 15 min.
   1.4. Collect the trypsin and cells into a 50 mL conical tube, rinse the plate with PBS, and collect remaining cells.
   1.5. Centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 min at 4°C.

2. Prepare macrophages for plating:
   2.1. Count macrophages using a hemocytometer.
   2.2. Resuspend macrophages in RPMI complete with M-CSF and pipet 1 mL into each well at a density of 25,000–100,000 cells/mL.
   2.3. Gently rock the plate to distribute the macrophages evenly.
   2.4. Incubate at 37°C with 5% CO2 for at least 24 h.

3. If not performing the phagocytosis assay within 2 days, feed the macrophages with additional RPMI complete with M-CSF every two to three days.

4. Collect tumor cells (if non-adherent cells, skip to 4.e):
   4.1. Aspirate cell medium.
   4.2. Wash tumor cell flask three times with PBS.
   4.3. Add trypsin 0.25% EDTA and incubate for 2–3 min at 37°C.
   4.4. Quench trypsin with RPMI complete and collect cells into a 15 mL conical tube.
   4.5. Centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
   4.6. Aspirate supernatant and resuspend tumor cells in HBSS.
   4.7. Repeat steps 4.6-4.8 twice more, and count cells during the second wash.

5. Optionally stain non-fluorescent tumor cells with CFSE or other dye after counting, following manufacturer's protocol.

6. Prepare cells for plating:
   6.1. Determine resuspension volume for desired tumor cell number per well, resuspend in RPMI complete with M-CSF.
   6.2. Keep tumor cells on ice.

7. Aspirate supernatant from the 12-well plates with reseeded macrophages.

8. Optionally wash the 12-well plates three times with PBS if the macrophages are pretreated.

9. Plate tumor cells onto macrophages:
   9.1. Prepare three replicate wells for each condition tested.
   9.2. Add 1 mL of 1× tumor cell solution per well for untreated, or 500 μL of 2× tumor cell and 500 μL of 2× treatment solution per well for treated conditions.
   9.3. Include macrophage-only and tumor cell-only wells as controls.
   9.4. After plating, gently rock the plate to distribute the cells.
   9.5. Incubate at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 18–24 h.

10. Prepare flow cytometry tubes with HBSS for each well.

11. Collect supernatant from each well into the corresponding tube.

12. Add trypsin 0.25% EDTA to each well and incubate for 15 min at 37°C.

13. Collect trypsinized cells into corresponding flow tubes, keeping plates and tubes on ice.

14. Centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 min at 4°C.

15. Prepare flow stain with anti-human or anti-mouse CD45 antibody.

16. Decant the supernatant from the flow tubes.

17. Add flow stain to the appropriate tubes and vortex.

18. Stain on ice for 15 min, protected from light.

19. Add 1% formalin to fix cells.

20. Store tubes at 4°C until flow cytometry analysis.
